content:
A compensation demand received by a company does not, by itself, establish who is liable or whether insurance applies. For a Moldovan business, start with three questions: what happened, who alleges harm, and which activity or property is connected with it. Verify answers using evidence rather than a generic policy name.

The search phrase legal liability insurance does not identify a single product for every company obligation. This article explains preparing records and distinguishing circumstances. It determines no litigation liability and confirms no solution's availability for an individual company.

Your property damage and someone else's loss are different

A damaged shop shelf concerns the owner's property. A demand for another person's item damaged in connection with shop activities is a separate claim. One incident can create both questions, but they require different documents. Do not combine categories in one estimate without explaining them.

For each item, record owner, incident location and alleged harm. Separate amounts paid from amounts merely requested. An invoice from a claimant is evidence in the file, not automatic confirmation that the company or an insurer owes the entire amount.

Describe actual activities

We provide services does not explain machinery repairs, event organization or cleaning at a client's premises. Describe operations, locations and participants. Include work on client sites, property taken into custody and subcontracting where applicable. A short accurate description is more useful than an unexplained activity label.

One firm may have several exposures. Selling products does not automatically describe installation; design is not execution. These distinctions help ask about general liability, professional indemnity or other contracts without assuming one policy covers everything the business does.

For example, a business that normally supplies equipment may also accept an installation request. Record that extra operation and the document authorizing it. The sales description alone would not tell a reviewer what the team actually did at the client site.

Identify the roles involved

Build a role list rather than collecting personal records. Identify the contracting company, client, premises owner and subcontractors. Check whether the demand addresses the entity in the documents. A trading brand on an entrance may differ from the legal company signing the agreement.

Initially use an anonymous summary instead of publishing names, identity records or medical details. Agree a confidential channel for necessary documents. Accurate identities may later matter, but distribution should remain limited to people with an actual role in the review.

A timeline is better than a rushed conclusion

Record separately the work date, discovery date, first complaint and notification to responsible people. Preserve original messages and document versions. An invoice date is not automatically an incident date without evidence. The difference may matter in contractual review and factual reconstruction.

Include uncertainties, such as cause unconfirmed pending a specialist report. This is more accurate than immediate blame. Technical investigation, legal review and insurance assessment are different activities. They should be coordinated without one being treated as a replacement for the others.

In a working chronology, an unknown discovery date can remain explicitly unknown while an invoice date is recorded separately. Ask the relevant person for the missing evidence rather than treating the only available date as an answer to every question.

Commercial agreements and policies are not the same

A client agreement may require limits or an insurance certificate. That does not establish insurer acceptance of every commercial obligation. Match client requirements with issued documents, checking declared activity, entities and dates. A page labelled certificate is not sufficient proof of every condition.

Ask a lawyer about indemnities, penalties or assuming another party's liability. Ask the insurer about their treatment under the actual policy wording. A commercial obligation must not be translated into a coverage promise simply because both documents mention liability.

Review the insurance documents

Start with subject and declared activity, then limits, excess, territory and exclusions. The premium is the amount paid for insurance. The excess is the share borne under contractual conditions. A policy limit is not the same as the amount any third party can demand.

Ask how limits work per event and over the period. Clarify defence costs, notification and known circumstances. These are document-check questions, not cover confirmed by this article. National Bank explanations concern general contract elements; your answer depends on the signed conditions.

Separate allegation, findings and amount requested

A complaint expresses its sender's position. A technical report may examine a damage mechanism, while a financial assessment proposes repair cost. Do not give each document more authority than it contains. Keep contradictions visible and seek specialist explanation rather than silently choosing the favourable version.

For requested amounts, list supporting records, currency and verification status. Avoid adding replacement estimates and repair invoices where they are alternatives for one item. Separate material damage, expenses and other demands without deciding here whether they are owed or insured.

Suppose a claimant sends both a replacement quotation and a repair estimate for the same object. Label them as alternatives until their purpose is clarified. Adding them without explanation would not show one established loss and could obscure the actual amount requested.

Customer property held temporarily needs a separate question

Workshops, warehouses and service firms may hold clients' property. Preserve handover records, descriptions and condition observations. A dated photograph helps organize facts but does not replace required documents or professional findings. Record why and when the property was received.

Mention custody explicitly in insurance questions. Do not assume general liability treats own, rented and accepted-for-work assets identically. Supply the same factual description to everyone assessing terms so differences in answers remain visible.

An illustrative claim file

A furniture installer receives a complaint about damage to the client's floor. A file might include the order, premises handover record, work description, complaint and existing images. This is a hypothetical organizational example, not an Insurance ING Broker SRL client or a liability finding.

The team separates furniture cost from the requested floor amount and identifies facts needing inspection. It does not promise payment from insurance before review. A coordinator tracks open questions and sends records through the agreed channel, keeping communications and versions.

Before a professional discussion

For preventive assessment, prepare one page of activities, sites, client categories, subcontractors and property held. Add known incidents in summary. Do not send the whole company archive before agreeing purpose and access. The necessary evidence can be selected once the actual review is clear.

For an existing incident, accurate facts and preservation come first. Insurance ING Broker SRL is a broker, not a court or claims-paying insurer. Explaining insurance questions does not replace litigation representation or technical expertise. Request the appropriate professional support for those tasks.

Services changed after signing

Additional instructions may change actual work at the client site. Equipment delivery could become installation absent from the original scope. Preserve requests and acceptance of changes. Do not base analysis solely on an initial quotation if the real work differed.

Also identify services abandoned or transferred to subcontractors. An updated description helps lawyers and insurance reviewers discuss the same facts. This does not mean every change is contractually accepted. It means assessment concerns actual operations without omissions.

Avoid contradictory versions

The site team may hold a report, accounting a budget and management a client letter. Give files names and dates and maintain a list. If two records describe one item differently, record the contradiction and who can explain it rather than silently selecting the beneficial version.

Link photographs to their stage and location without adding unsupported causal conclusions. Keep the transmission message with client documents. Organization does not determine liability, but reduces the risk of treating a provisional estimate as a final finding or an old schedule as current.

For example, keep a provisional site report identifiable as provisional when a later specialist report arrives. Link both to the same object and preserve the received messages. A short management summary should identify the unresolved difference rather than silently present the earlier observation as a final technical conclusion.

Frequently asked questions

Is every complaint an insured loss?

No conclusion follows solely from a complaint. Facts, liability and policy conditions require separate assessment. Preserve the demand without converting it into a payment promise.

Is professional indemnity the same as general liability?

Do not treat names as equivalent. Describe services, possible harm and circumstances, then clarify each contract's subject. Some activities require profession-specific questions.

What if the client requests a higher limit?

Compare the requirement with existing documents and discuss changes before confirming compliance. A client's request does not automatically amend a policy or establish extension availability.

Can I decide who is at fault?

Record facts you know, but legal conclusions require competent review. Separate observations, technical findings and legal positions so the file remains accurate and traceable.
